then.text: There's a trainer who came to King John's... I'll be humming it for weeks. Thank you.
Ruairí beaten and the market laughing! That's a limerick doing its job. Here: a Munster scrum cap, and a scrap of Limerick lace for luck. You're a poet now. God help us.
Off to the Milk Market with it! Ruairí the bard holds court there. Recite it to the crowd, then see him off.
'A young trainer who came to King John's.' Lovely. Now. Line two has to rhyme with 'John's' and keep the bounce.
Line two: 'Brought a team made of...'
'Ducks and of swans.' Perfect. Lines three and four are short and rhyme with each other. I'll give you three: 'They hissed at the gate,'

options: And one bit a guard on the bum
Which upset the man on duty

then.text: Ha! Now the last line. It has to rhyme with John's and swans, and it has to land the joke.

options: So they all went home for a nap.
And they guard it themselves now with wands.
And King John said a very rude word.

then.text: 'A young trainer who came to King John's / Brought a team made of ducks and of swans. / They hissed at the gate, / And a guard yelled, "Ye're late!" / And they guard it themselves now with wands.'
Wands! It's nonsense. It's perfect. Now go and try it on the Milk Market crowd. If Ruairí the bard doesn't heckle you off the crate, it's a keeper.

else.text: The rude word, I'll allow. But it has to rhyme, pet. Have a think and come back.
Ha! Filthy. And it doesn't rhyme. Save it for the second verse. Have a think and come back.
It doesn't rhyme with John's, does it? Say them out loud. Go on. Have a think and come back to me.

then.text: King John's Castle first. The guide has a first line for you; he's been sitting on it for years.

else.text: Welcome to the Poet's Rest. Tonight's limerick night, and I'm a verse short. Five lines: one, two and five rhyme; three and four are short and rhyme with each other.
Nobody can prove the limerick comes from Limerick. We've decided not to let that stop us.
Will you write one with me? Get a first line from the guide at King John's Castle. He's been dying to be asked.

poets_quizmaster.text: Pub quiz, every night bar Sunday. Questions on the whole of these islands, and a few on Limerick, of course.

poets_regular.text: There was an old man from Thomondgate / Who drank till a quarter past eight. / He went home to bed, / With a hat on his head... I forget the rest. It's very good, the rest.
